note: The voice command registry: the one place the Python router and the browser
executor agree on what speech may do. The router turns this into the tool
schemas it offers the model; the browser turns it into the executor's switch.
A test on each side asserts its own half covers exactly these names, so a
command added here fails loudly on whichever side forgot it rather than
silently becoming an intent nothing performs.
`effect` is the operator-visible consequence, and it is what decides whether
a spoken confirmation is required -- not the command's name:
view    changes what is on screen and nothing else; freely reversible.
compute spends from the gateway budget or GPU time; reversible but costly.
audit   writes an operator decision into the record. NOT reversible.
Voice is admin-level by team decision (see logs/step_stt_development_logs.md
S6): every command here is reachable by speech. `confirm` is the single
safeguard left, and `voice.confirm_audit_commands: false` in goru.yaml turns
